primitives.name: Pullback Transformation
primitives.verbatim_quote: 39] A transformation T from X into Y assigns in an obvious way a function f on X to every function g on Y;f is defined by f(x) = g(T(x)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'transformation from X to Y', 'f': 'function on X', 'g': 'function on Y', 'x': 'element of X', 'y': 'element of Y'}
primitives.assumptions: T is a well-defined mapping between sets X and Y; g is a function on Y.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T is not surjective or g lacks domain coverage.

layer2.mapping: Maps functions on codomain Y to functions on domain X via composition gT = g∘T.
layer2.telemetry: Verification via equality of compositions (gT)(x) = g(T(x))

primitives.name: Measurable Transformation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Motivated by the special case in which Y is the real line, we shall say that T is a measurable transformation if the inverse image of every measurable set is measurable.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'sigma-ring on Y', 'S': 'sigma-ring on X', 'F': 'measurable set in T'}
primitives.assumptions: X and Y are measurable spaces with associated sigma-rings S and T.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When inverse image T⁻¹(F) fails to belong to S for some F ∈ T.

layer2.mapping: Preserves structure of measurable sets under inverse image operation.
layer2.telemetry: Verification via inclusion T⁻¹(T) ⊆ S where T⁻¹(T) is the preimage ring.

primitives.name: Composition Equivalence
primitives.verbatim_quote: The following statements are mutually equivalent: (a) x0 ε {x: (gT)(x) ε M}, (b) g(T(x0)) ε M, (c) if y0 = T(x0), then g(yo) ε M, and (d) T(x0) ε { y: g(y) ε M}.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'g': 'function on Y', 'T': 'transformation from X to Y', 'M': 'subset of range of g', 'x₀': 'element of X', 'y₀': 'element of Y'}
primitives.assumptions: g is a function on Y, T is a transformation from X to Y, M is a subset of g's codomain.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When T is not injective or g is undefined on T(x₀).

layer2.mapping: Equates pointwise evaluation of composite function with set membership in image.
layer2.telemetry: Equivalence verified by checking mutual containment of sets {x : (gT)(x) ∈ M} and T⁻¹({y : g(y) ∈ M})

The core idea revolves around the duality between transformations and their induced actions on functions. Given a transformation T: X → Y, each function g on Y yields a pullback function f = gT on X such that f(x) = g(T(x)). This establishes a canonical map from functions on Y to functions on X. The equivalence of statements (a)-(d) demonstrates that evaluating gT at x₀ is equivalent to checking whether T(x₀) lies in the preimage of M under g. This foundational result underpins measure theory, particularly when defining measurable transformations as those preserving sigma-algebras under inverse images. The failure mode occurs when T lacks sufficient regularity or when g is not defined on the range of T. In GSI, this translates to probabilistic updating through measurable mappings; in GSE, it governs state transitions in dynamical systems.
